rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3: own UAV survey (Parrot Anafi, 24 May 2019) over a 0.78 ha maize field in NE Italy, own classification runs (MLC, ANN, OBIA) and nine own prescription maps. Q2: Section 3 and Table 2: area to be sprayed as share of the 7832 m2 field ranges from 14.59% to 2.18% (MLC), 18.92% to 3.75% (ANN) and 15.82% to 3.49% (OBIA) depending on cell size and threshold, versus full-field spraying. Q7: Section 4: authors state from their results that smaller grid cells gave lower treated areas, so the detection scale must be matched to the spraying technology available (section or nozzle-level control), and that such sprayers are not yet widely adopted in Italy. Q8: Section 4: authors state that no spraying was carried out, that field trials are needed to validate the maps under operational conditions, and that cost-effectiveness data for Italian systems are missing; single field and single survey date.
rows.notes: The study reports potential (map-based) reductions of the area to be sprayed; no herbicide was applied and no weed-control or yield outcome was measured, so the evidence is on treated-area reduction only, not on actual weed control efficacy. Classification accuracies are taken from Mattivi et al. (2021), not re-assessed here. The passage misstates several points: the crop is maize, not a vegetable crop; the figures 2.18-18.92% are the share of the field still to be sprayed (i.e. 81-98% reduction), not the amount of reduction; and the study explicitly did not compare algorithm efficiency, noting only that ANN had higher sensitivity and produced larger treated areas. Q3: one method (RGB UAV image classification with three algorithms). Q4: weed pixel share per cell is computed but no independent ground measurement of weed distribution is reported in this paper; answered no. Q5/Q6: one field, one crop, one site, one date. Q9: no dispersion or uncertainty measures, only deterministic areas.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study builds on classification outputs validated in a prior paper (Mattivi et al., 2021) and only adds the prescription-map / treated-area scenario analysis.
